sub_answers.text: A railway and road extension to Nusaybin in 1918 intensified Kurdish southward immigration into Syria’s foothills and plains along rivers. [d3821855s1p0] In the 1920s, after failed Kurdish rebellions in Kemalist Turkey, there was a large Kurdish migration to Syria’s Jazira province, with an estimate of 25,000 Kurds fleeing to Syria. [d3821855s1p0] In 1929, a further wave of refugees arrived, and French authorities continued to allow Kurdish migration into the Mandate, with Jazira Kurdish villages numbering between 700 and 800 by 1939. [d3821855s1p0] In Damascus, Kurdish communities were present by the early 20th century (around 12,000 Kurds), including the neighborhood Rukn al-Din (formerly Hayy al Akrad). [d3821855s1p0]
